hypothesis: Same build as exp-rayon-io, re-measured on the boxes as they are now. The boxes were idle-stopped and restarted (likely new physical hosts) between exp-rayon-io and the CPU-feature runs, whose c8g gains (~2.5%) did not stack. If this re-measure also lands near 6.55s on c8g, those gains were host change.
llm_commentary: m8azn.xlarge (AMD EPYC Turin, Zen 5 at 5.0 GHz, 4 vCPUs, priced like c8a.2xlarge): stock main 6.46s [6.40/6.50/6.47] → champion 5.51s [5.50/5.59/5.45] on the same boot, -14.7%, about the same relative gain as c8a (-14.2%), consistent with identical Zen 5 cores and codegen. On half the vCPUs it ties stock m9g (6.46s) and lands just behind champion c8i (5.50s), but it trails c8a (4.76s) and m9g (4.59s) with the champion: the light phase's 64 client connections and the heavy phase's 8 concurrent calls share 4 vCPUs with the oha client, so clock speed cannot make up for half the cores. At ~$0.00063 per run it is also more expensive per run than m9g ($0.00050). For a latency-bound single-call workload it could win; for this throughput benchmark the 8-vCPU boxes are better.
